title: The Nephites advance
summary: In the three hundred and sixty-third year, Nephite armies go up from the land Desolation to battle the Lamanites.

explicit_facts.text: In the three hundred and sixty-third year, the Nephites went up with their armies to battle the Lamanites, out of the land Desolation.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Armed groups moving out from the land Desolation toward one another.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of the armies, weapons, terrain, weather, and composition of the march.

narration.text: the Nephites did go up with their armies

prohibited_inventions: Named individual commanders or specific battle actions not stated in this verse.

title: The fall of city Desolation
summary: The Nephite armies are driven back to the land of Desolation. While they are weary, a fresh Lamanite army comes upon them. After a sore battle, the Lamanites take possession of the city Desolation, slay many Nephites, and take many prisoners. The remainder flee and join the inhabitants of city Teancum, which lies by the seashore near city Desolation.

explicit_facts.text: The Nephite armies were driven back to the land of Desolation.
While the Nephites were weary, a fresh Lamanite army came upon them, and they had a sore battle.
The Lamanites took possession of city Desolation, slew many Nephites, and took many prisoners.
The remainder fled and joined the inhabitants of city Teancum, which lay by the seashore near city Desolation.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The weary Nephite armies may appear fatigued.
The remainder’s flight to Teancum follows the battle rather than occurring simultaneously with it.
unspecified_visual_details: The cities’ layouts, clothing, weapons, and shoreline appearance are not described.

narration.text: and they had a sore battle
And the remainder did flee and join the inhabitants of the city Teancum.

prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the armies with figures or eras absent from these verses.
Do not invent individual actions, dialogue, or prisoner identities.
Do not depict gore.

title: The Nephite armies are smitten
summary: The armies of the Nephites went up unto the Lamanites and began to be smitten.

explicit_facts.text: The armies of the Nephites began to be smitten because they went up unto the Lamanites.
The passage teaches that God's judgments will overtake the wicked, that the wicked are punished by the wicked, and that the wicked stir up hearts unto bloodshed.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The Nephite armies may be shown advancing toward the Lamanites and beginning to be repelled, without graphic injury.
unspecified_visual_details: Terrain, clothing, weapons, and the armies' appearances are not described.

narration.text: And it was because the armies of the Nephites went up unto the Lamanites that they began to be smitten;
But, behold, the judgments of God will overtake the wicked;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Verse 5 is a teaching, not a narrated visible divine judgment.
prohibited_inventions: An identified speaker or narrator
A visible divine judgment
A separate scene of bloodshed
Graphic wounds or gore

title: The battle resumes
summary: After the three hundred and sixty-sixth year passed, the Lamanites came again upon the Nephites to battle. The Nephites did not repent and continued in wickedness. Blood and carnage were among both peoples; every heart was hardened, and they delighted in shedding blood continually.

explicit_facts.text: After the three hundred and sixty-sixth year passed, the Lamanites came again upon the Nephites to battle.
The Nephites did not repent of the evil they had done and persisted in wickedness.
Blood and carnage were among both peoples; every heart was hardened, and they delighted in shedding blood continually.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The renewed battle may be depicted through non-graphic combat action.

explicit_facts.text: The verse compares the wickedness among this people with that among the children of Lehi and the house of Israel, according to the words of the Lord.

title: Desolation and Teancum
summary: The Lamanites take Desolation because they outnumber the Nephites. They then march against Teancum, drive out its inhabitants, take many prisoners, including women and children, and offer sacrifices to their idol gods.

explicit_facts.text: The Lamanites took Desolation because they outnumbered the Nephites.
The Lamanites marched against Teancum, drove out its inhabitants, and took many prisoners, including women and children.
The Lamanites offered sacrifices to their idol gods.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The taking of Desolation precedes the march against Teancum; they should not be shown as simultaneous.
